Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).Affected_Part: Leaves, Shoots, Fruits, Roots, Entire Plant
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).Environment: Warm subtropical and tropical climates (20–35°C). Disease spreads rapidly where Asian citrus psyllids are abundant.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).Spread: Primarily transmitted by the Asian Citrus Psyllid (Diaphorina citri). It can also spread through infected nursery stock and grafting material.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).Description: Huanglongbing (HLB), also known as Citrus Greening, is one of the most destructive citrus diseases worldwide. The bacterium infects the phloem tissue, disrupting nutrient transport, resulting in yellow shoots, deformed fruits and eventual tree decline.

Age_Cycle.Early: Leaves develop blotchy yellow mottling and asymmetric chlorosis.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Shoots become yellow, fruits remain small, green and misshapen.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Tree decline, heavy fruit drop, root deterioration and eventual death.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Symptoms usually appear several months after infection, while tree decline may take several years.

Treatment: There is currently no cure for infected trees.
Remove severely infected trees to reduce disease spread.
Maintain balanced nutrition to improve tree health.
Organic_Treatment: Release beneficial predators such as lady beetles and parasitic wasps
Yellow sticky traps for psyllid monitoring
Recommended_Actions: Inspect citrus trees every week for psyllids and yellow shoots.
Immediately report suspected HLB outbreaks to local agricultural authorities if required.
Use only certified disease-free planting material.
